criteria.description: The v2 judge prompt is authored as a versioned in-module constant carrying a version identifier/tag. The v2 text explicitly states that matching topic/shape/keywords is insufficient and that an explanation substituting different list members, a different mechanism, or contradicting specifics is NOT covered even if fluent and topically adjacent. Test passes under the verifier command.

criteria.description: Truncation detection: when the parsed verdict count is less than the claim count, the module detects the mismatch and triggers a bounded retry; if a subsequent response is complete, the correct full verdict set is returned. criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test with a mocked client whose first response has fewer verdicts than claims and whose second is complete asserts: model called twice, final returned verdict set is correct and full-count. criteria.description: Malformed model output (invalid JSON) triggers a bounded retry; if all attempts remain malformed, a typed error from the existing hierarchy (VerdictParseError and subclasses) is raised rather than returning a partial/garbage verdict. criteria.description: A pure function union_coverage(verdict_sets) is added to coverage_judge.py that accepts an iterable of verdict SETS as produced by the module's own judge — i.e. the full verdict object shape {verdicts: [{claim_id, covered, turns}, ...], judged_at, model, judge_prompt_hash} returned by judge_coverage (accepting the bare per-claim verdict list additionally is allowed but the full-object shape MUST be supported) — and returns a dict with keys covered_ids (a JSON-serializable list of claim ids) and percentage (a number). It performs NO file I/O, NO model/LLM calls, and no network access.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test in tests/test_coverage_judge.py imports union_coverage and calls it with the ACTUAL output shape of judge_coverage (built by calling judge_coverage with the model call mocked, or by constructing the identical {verdicts:[...], judged_at, model, judge_prompt_hash} dict) so it composes with Sprint 1's judge; asserts the return has keys covered_ids (a list) and percentage; runs with zero network calls under `uv run --with pytest pytest tests/test_coverage_judge.py -q`.

criteria.description: union_coverage merges covered claim ids by UNION across sessions: a claim id is in covered_ids if it is covered in ANY session, even if not covered in others (overlapping and disjoint cases both merge correctly). covered_ids is order-insensitive and de-duplicated.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test supplies two verdict sets where covered ids differ/overlap (e.g. session A covers {c1,c2} and marks c3 not-covered; session B covers {c2,c3}) and asserts set(covered_ids) == {c1,c2,c3} with no duplicates.

criteria.description: union_coverage computes percentage at read time (derived, not stored) as: (count of distinct covered claim ids) divided by (count of distinct claim ids judged across ALL merged verdict sets, i.e. every claim appearing in any set whether covered or not) times 100, using a single fixed, documented rounding convention.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic tests: (a) a terminating case where 3 of 4 distinct claims are covered => percentage == 75.0 (exact equality), confirming the denominator counts all distinct judged claim ids (covered + not-covered), not just covered ones; (b) a NON-terminating case that actually exercises the rounding convention — e.g. 2 of 3 distinct claims covered => assert percentage EQUALS the module's documented rounded value for 66.666… (whatever fixed convention the module fixes, e.g. round to 1 decimal => 66.7 or round to 2 => 66.67), so an absent/broken rounding rule cannot pass silently.

criteria.description: union_coverage handles edge cases without raising: empty input (no verdict sets, or verdict sets whose verdict lists are empty) yields covered_ids == [] and percentage == 0.0 (no divide-by-zero); a single-session input returns exactly that session's covered ids and its own percentage.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic tests: (a) union_coverage([]) and union_coverage over sets with empty verdict lists return covered_ids == [] and percentage == 0.0 without raising; (b) a single-session input reproduces that session's covered ids (order-insensitive) and its exact percentage.
